RJ Mitte’s “Breaking Bad” co-stars and loved ones gathered for the late actor’s celebration of life ceremony in Los Angeles on Saturday.

Aaron Paul, Bryan Cranston and Bob Odenkirk were among the attendees paying tribute to Mitte at Hope Lutheran Church in Hollywood, per photos obtained by Page Six.

Jonathan Banks and Raymond Cruz were also photographed with other friends, including Gilles Marini.

Photographs from inside the venue showed a massive photo of Mitte surrounded by floral arrangements.

An invitation asked attendees to join in the church service at 1:30 p.m. Saturday, followed by a reception at The Remix Room in Hollywood from 3:30 p.m. to 7:30 p.m.

Mitte died by suicide in Texas on Oct. 12. He was 34.

“It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte,” his spokesperson wrote in a statement to Page Six.

“RJ Mitte was best known for his role as Walter ‘Flynn’ White Jr. on AMC’s critically acclaimed, award-winning series ‘Breaking Bad.’ Drawing from his own experience living with cerebral palsy, Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion.”

Mitte played the role of Walter White’s son, portrayed by Cranston, on “Breaking Bad” for five seasons from 2008 to 2013.

Cranston mourned Mitte via an emotional Instagram tribute, writing that it was “especially devastating to hear that he took his own life.”

“Why?” the 70-year-old actor wrote. “We were texting each other just a few weeks ago — figuring out when we could meet for lunch. I don’t know if that lunch would have changed his future.”

Weeks before he died, Mitte appeared on the “Brownsville in Motion” podcast, sharing how he wanted his life to be at the age of 50.

“I would hope to stay true to what I believe and to what I want to achieve,” he said. “And not be a grumpy middle-aged person … A curmudgeon.”

At the time, Mitte, who was diagnosed with cerebral palsy at the age of 3, explained he had “a lot of hip pain,” so he believed he would be “all shriveled” as he aged.

Additionally, Mittle expressed his hopes for The Mitte Foundation, a non-profit organization with a mission to help those with disabilities.

If you or someone you know is affected by any of the issues raised in this story, call the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 1-800-273-TALK (8255) or text Crisis Text Line at 741741.

California’s next insurance commissioner is promising a sweeping overhaul of the state’s embattled insurance industry, including a first-of-its-kind public disaster insurance program that would guarantee wildfire coverage for homeowners.

Jane Kim, a former San Francisco supervisor who defeated fellow Democrat Ben Allen in the race for insurance commissioner, declared victory Friday after campaigning on a plan to wrestle control of wildfire coverage away from private insurers and create a state-run, nonprofit alternative.

“We are here to say no more. We are going to make insurance work for us again,” Kim told supporters at her victory event.

“We are going to take on this $3-trillion industry because they have been profiting for way too long by raising our premiums, canceling our coverage and fighting our claims.”

Kim’s proposal, dubbed “Natural Disaster Insurance for All,” would separate wildfire coverage from traditional homeowners insurance policies and move it into a public, nonprofit fund.

The program would make wildfire insurance available to every current California homeowner, with premiums going toward providing coverage rather than executive compensation, shareholders or corporate advertising.

“The idea is that every current homeowner would be covered, and it would be a nonprofit fund where premiums don’t have to go to CEO pay, shareholders and Super Bowl ads,” Kim said.

The ambitious proposal comes as California grapples with an increasingly severe homeowners insurance crisis, with major carriers retreating from the state and residents struggling to find affordable coverage.

Seven of California’s largest property insurers have limited or paused new homeowners policies in the state, shrinking the private insurance marketplace as wildfire risks and rising costs continue to threaten coverage.

Homeowners insurance premiums have surged 84% since 2020, according to Stanford research, while enrollment in the state’s FAIR Plan — the insurer of last resort for homeowners unable to secure coverage through traditional companies — has nearly tripled.

The plan now covers roughly 5% of California homes, up from less than 2%, highlighting how the insurance crunch has spread beyond traditionally fire-prone communities and into the broader housing market.

Kim’s proposed public fund would effectively create a separate safety net for wildfire coverage, rather than forcing homeowners to rely entirely on private insurers.

But turning the proposal into reality could prove difficult, requiring cooperation from state lawmakers and community leaders to establish the program and determine how it would be funded and administered.

“This office is not a dictatorship. We’re going to have to work with community leaders across the state to make our big ideas possible,” Kim said.

Despite the hurdles, the incoming commissioner-elect said she expects to make progress on affordability and availability during her first year in office.

“I really believe we’re going to have some wins in our first year because there is a lot of work that can be done to make insurance more affordable, more available and more fair,” she said.

Kim, 49, secured approximately 53% of the vote to Allen’s 47%, according to the Associated Press. Her victory margin has grown to approximately 400,000 votes as additional ballots were tallied.

Allen called Kim to congratulate her on the victory Friday morning before she announced the results to supporters at San Francisco’s Dolores Park.

The win hands Kim responsibility for overseeing one of California’s most troubled industries at a time when homeowners are facing mounting premiums, canceled policies and fewer options for protecting their properties.

Her proposed nonprofit disaster insurance system would represent a major departure from the state’s traditional insurance model — and one of the most consequential tests of her incoming administration.

news.content: پوشش های بیشتری را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. کمیسیونر بعدی بیمه کالیفرنیا نوید یک بازنگری گسترده در صنعت بیمه درگیر این ایالت را می دهد، از جمله اولین برنامه بیمه عمومی بلایای طبیعی در نوع خود که پوشش آتش سوزی برای مالکان خانه را تضمین می کند. جین کیم، ناظر سابق سانفرانسیسکو که بن آلن همکار دموکرات خود را در رقابت برای کمیسیون بیمه شکست داد، روز جمعه پس از مبارزات انتخاباتی برای مبارزه با کنترل پوشش آتش‌سوزی‌های جنگلی به دور از بیمه‌گران خصوصی و ایجاد یک جایگزین غیرانتفاعی دولتی و دولتی اعلام پیروزی کرد. بزرگ‌ترین اخبار، نظر و فرهنگ شکل‌دهنده کالیفرنیا در حال حاضر. لطفاً یک ایمیل معتبر ارائه دهید. با کلیک کردن در بالا، با شرایط استفاده و خط‌مشی رازداری موافقت می‌کنید. "ما این صنعت 3 تریلیون دلاری را به عهده می‌گیریم زیرا آنها برای مدت طولانی با افزایش حق بیمه ما، لغو پوشش ما و مبارزه با ادعاهای ما سود می‌برند." پیشنهاد کیم که "بیمه بلایای طبیعی برای همه" نامیده شد، پوشش آتش سوزی را از بیمه نامه های سنتی مالکان خانه جدا می کند و آن را به یک صندوق عمومی و غیرانتفاعی منتقل می کند. این برنامه بیمه آتش سوزی جنگلی را برای هر صاحب خانه فعلی کالیفرنیا در دسترس قرار می دهد، با حق بیمه به جای غرامت اجرایی، سهامداران یا صاحبان سهام تبلیغات فعلی هستند.

Take Sunday afternoon, for instance. Iona didn’t just struggle to inbound the ball against the press, but when it did, getting it past halfcourt felt like an accomplishment. The Johnnies forced 19 turnovers and turned them into 26 points in a 104-65 beatdown at the Garden. By halftime, Iona had committed 15 turnovers.

St. John’s pressure helped them get out to a big lead in the season opener against Monmouth and was a big part of their exhibition finale against Texas.

While Pitino has said this team has a lot of learning to do in terms of getting familiar with one another and improving on basic fundamentals, it has the length and athleticism to be a very strong pressing team. Quinn Ellis and Tounde Yessoufou each had three steals to lead the defensive charge.

St. John’s had its way with the Gaels from the start, scoring 14 of the game’s first 31 points. They closed the first half on a 21-4 run, and went into the break up by 31.

Pitino wanted to see them get up more 3-point attempts, and Ian Jackson came out firing from deep, making his first two attempts. St. John’s finished with 13 made 3-pointers. Yessoufu had four of them, and tallied 23 points, seven rebounds and two blocks. Jackson had 17 and Keyshawn Hall added 13. Ellis notched 11 assists, along with seven points and five rebounds.

Forward Babacar Sane (ankle) didn’t play. Godson Okokoh, a four-star forward recruit from Bella Vista College Prep (Ariz.), was in attendance for the game.

Life-saving organs including the “gift of sight’’ were donated by tragic slain Brooklyn jogger Katie Suarez to three New Yorkers and a resident of Florida between the ages of 12 and 75, officials revealed Sunday.

“LiveOnNY is humbled and honored to be the stewards of these precious gifts of life so that Katie’s legacy and others may live on,” said Leonard Achan, the president & CEO of the organ-donation group.

“Ms. Suarez saved the lives of four people with five of her organs to those waiting on the national transplant waitlist,’’ the organization said in a statement to The Post.

“LiveOnNY’s ensured that Katie’s gifts of life arrived to transplant centers where four recipients who were between the ages of 12 and 75-years-old were successfully transplanted. Three of the recipients were in New York and one was in Florida.

“Ms. Suarez, a bank teller and graduate of Brooklyn College, was able to donate her heart, both kidneys, a liver and pancreas. She also gave the gift of sight.”

Suarez was jogging on the Shore Parkway Greenway on her way to meet up with her parents on the evening of Oct. 30 when she was stabbed to death in the neck, allegedly by ex-NYPD Officer and current Brooklyn elementary school paraprofessional Sayed Mohassib.

The suspect, 27, allegedly told cops he had gone to the Bath Beach promenade with a knife over deranged fears that his family was being threatened.

The attack was apparently random, law-enforcement sources have said.

Taylor Swift and Karlie Kloss reunited at the Kansas City Chiefs game Sunday, months after rekindling their friendship following years of rumored tension.

The pop superstar, 36, and the supermodel, 33, were spotted watching Swift’s husband, Travis Kelce, and his teammates take on the New York Jets at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri.

Taylor’s mom, Andrea Swift, and Travis’ mom, Donna Kelce, were also pictured in the suite.

The former BFFs appeared to be in good spirits as they watched the action from a VIP suite during the first half of the game.

In photos from the outing, Taylor, who wore a red top, was seen smiling and chatting with fellow spectators, while Kloss flashed a grin nearby.

The surprise reunion comes four months after Kloss and her husband, Joshua Kushner, attended Taylor and Travis’ star-studded wedding at Madison Square Garden in New York City.

The model’s appearance at the July nuptials raised eyebrows after years of speculation that she and the “Cruel Summer” singer had fallen out.

Ahead of the wedding, reports suggested Kloss would be left off the guest list due to their strained relationship.

However, an insider subsequently told TMZ that the former friends had put their differences aside, paving the way for Kloss to attend the lavish celebration.

Taylor and Kloss were once practically inseparable after striking up a friendship in 2013, when the Grammy winner performed at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show.

The pair quickly became fixtures in each other’s lives, frequently stepping out together in New York City, attending basketball games and even posing for a joint Vogue cover in 2015.

Kloss was also a prominent member of Taylor’s famous celebrity “squad.”

However, feud rumors surfaced in 2018 when Taylor missed both of Kloss’ wedding ceremonies to Kushner.

Page Six reported in 2019 that Kloss had allegedly taken advantage of Taylor’s hospitality by inviting friends to the singer’s home without permission.

Neither woman has publicly confirmed the reason for their apparent falling-out.

In August 2023, Kloss surprised Swifties when she attended the singer’s Eras Tour stop in Los Angeles.

news.originalContent:
The GOP suffered a loss, but it is hardly a historic one. A party in power has always been held to account in the midterms.

Republican strategist, TV host and writer.

On Tuesday, the United States held midterm elections. Every one of the 435 seats in the US House of Representatives was up for election and 35 of the 100 US Senate seats were on the ballot.

The result of the elections was overwhelmingly in favour of the Democratic Party, or the blue team, as the US media has taken to referring to them. It was a blue wave. A blue tsunami. Democrats flipped at least 40 House seats and seven Senate seats. It was a clear message to Washington that much of the US is unhappy with the direction the country is headed.

Texas had not elected a Democrat in a statewide race for more than 30 years. Democrats dominated in Texas. Kansas hadn’t sent a Democrat to the Senate since 1932. Come the first week of January, there will be one representing it. Susan Collins, the powerful Republican chair of the Senate Committee on Appropriations and the most bipartisan voting Republican in the US Senate had been Maine’s senator for 30 years. She was voted out. The depth and breadth of the Democratic victory stunned many.

The war with Iran clearly had an impact. It wasn’t the conflict itself nearly as much as the economic impact it has had on the average American. Virtually every American uses an automobile and the price of petrol has skyrocketed during the war. The high fuel prices have impacted every other segment of the economy because nearly every product, especially food and grocery items, is delivered using the roadway system, which, of course, means petrol and diesel prices add to their cost.

The Democrats taking control of both the House and the Senate will dramatically change the next two years in Washington. They will restore the oversight functions of Congress and will investigate Trump and his team for countless violations, real or imagined. Congressional priorities will change. Impeachment will be a word that is commonly used again. If a vacancy occurs on the Supreme Court, the president will have a much more difficult time filling it. The impact of the elections is very real.

Is it historic though? In a word, no.

Losing seats to the opposition party is actually quite common in the midterms. Dozens of House races are still being counted, so the final tally may yet grow, but since World War II there have been at least seven midterm elections with seat losses comparable to or larger than what the Republicans have experienced so far in 2026: 1946, 1958, 1966, 1974, 1994, 2010 and 2018 when President Donald Trump’s party lost about 40 House seats in his first midterm.

The largest midterm loss belongs to President Barack Obama’s party in 2010. The Democrats lost 63 House seats and six seats in the Senate. The Democrats would then lose nine seats in the US Senate in the midterm elections held during Obama’s second term.

The Democrats under President Bill Clinton also took a beating in 1994 when the opposition Republicans gained 54 seats in the House, taking a majority for the first time in a generation, and flipping eight seats in the Senate.

The pundits at the time wondered aloud if it was the end of the Democratic Party. The losses were staggering. Both presidents, however, went on to govern effectively and find ways to work with the opposition. In fact, Clinton worked with the Republican Congress to pass the first balanced budget in memory. In that case, the split in government forced them to work together and produced a benefit to the American people.

None of this is new. President Harry Truman’s Democrats lost 55 House seats and 12 Senate seats in 1946. President Dwight Eisenhower’s Republicans took it on the chin in 1958, losing 48 House seats and 13 Senate seats. Presidents Lyndon Johnson, Gerald Ford and George HW Bush all took big losses. Even Ronald Reagan lost 26 House seats in his first midterm elections.

The point is the American public has always demanded accountability from Washington. No one should be surprised that at a time when only 14 percent of Americans think Congress is doing a good job and the prices for basic necessities are increasing, Americans demand change. They have done it over and over, regardless of the party in power.

The next logical question is where do we go from here? Is Trump’s reign as leader of the GOP over? Has he lost his influence?

There will not be a great deal of time spent trying to decipher what went wrong. Both Trump and Vice President JD Vance have already acknowledged the war in Iran and its economic effects are the primary reasons for the loss. This acknowledgement will hasten the healing process within the party, as will the need to push through a number of agenda items together in the remaining weeks the Republicans have control of Congress.

Because the US Constitution limits a president to two terms, any time any president enters his final two years, he is known as a lame duck. His influence, while still enormous simply by the reality of the office, begins to wane. The closer it gets to the end of his final term the less influence he has, particularly on the domestic agenda. Many presidents spend the majority of their time near the end of their term on foreign policy.

As of January 3, Democrats will set the agenda on Capitol Hill. They will control every committee. They will control virtually every vote. Congress controls the purse strings, so their impact is large, but don’t count Trump out yet.

His personality and his outward embrace of even the most difficult conflicts are unique. Whether in business, in election wins and losses, in courtroom clashes or in international affairs, Trump doesn’t back down. Admittedly this sometimes works to his detriment, but it is a trait that will likely serve him well as he battles with a Democratic-controlled Congress.

The president has veto authority over any legislation Congress passes. Rather than sign the legislation, he can reject it. If he rejects it, two-thirds of both the House and the Senate must vote to override his veto or else the legislation does not become law.

If Trump feels the Democrats are pushing an agenda too radical or too far left, he will wield the veto pen with great regularity.

Ideally the two sides understand the power each holds, and they will work together, as did a Republican-dominated Congress and Democratic President Clinton. If they do work together, all Americans will benefit. If each side digs in and refuses to compromise, it will be a long, unproductive two years.

Speaking of two years, 2028 is the next presidential election, and the question of who will be the nominee for each party is already being kicked around – and, in particular, how these midterm elections will impact the potential Republican candidates like Vance or Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

The stark reality is that two years is an eternity in politics. Anything can happen, despite the Republican defeat on Tuesday. The biggest question is whether the American public will be feeling “Trump fatigue” during the 2028 presidential election season.

If the public has grown weary of team Trump, anyone affiliated with his administration may be tainted goods and face a bigger challenge getting the party’s nomination. Vance, Rubio and others directly tied to him have the greatest name recognition right now, but that may prove to be baggage rather than an advantage.

Outsiders such as a state governor or a past political figure may generate public enthusiasm for a different direction. The list is long. Even Trump has said his party has a deep bench, and it’s true.

Trying to predict the 2028 nominee now, in such a volatile political time and with two years to go, while entertaining, is a fool’s errand.

Some in the media have begun to write the Republican Party’s obituary after Tuesday’s losses. The final numbers are not yet in, and in the Senate, the seven seats already lost exceed the six Obama’s party gave up in 2010.

Still, history shows that parties and presidents have come back from setbacks of this scale before, as Obama and Clinton both did. Trump and the Republicans can do the same.

A version of this piece was first published by Al Jazeera Arabic.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

news.originalContent:
Alcaraz bagged a 7-6 (7/5), 7-5 straight sets for an elusive Paris crown before the year-end ATP Finals.

Carlos Alcaraz has gained a measure of revenge on Ben Shelton as the seven-time Grand Slam champion beat the American 7-6 (7/5), 7-5 to win the Paris Masters for the first time.

In defeating the man who ended his US Open title defence earlier this season, the 23-year-old claimed the ninth 1000-level title of his career on Sunday.

Unlike their five-set quarterfinal epic in New York two months ago, the clash in Paris lasted just under two hours.

“Coming here every year, not finding my best tennis but we never gave up,” Alcaraz said after being handed the trophy for the first time by former Paris Masters winner Boris Becker.

“We had really painful losses here and we always said try again,” the Spaniard  added with a smile.

Ahead of the ATP Finals, which run from November 15-22 in Turin, world number three Alcaraz now holds five tour-level titles this year – only the injured Jannik Sinner has more with six.

Coming into Paris on the back of winning the 500-level title in Vienna, Alcaraz has won his last nine matches.

In Italy, he will be seeking a first coronation at the season-ender.

After winning two French Opens and now the Paris Masters, Alcaraz is undefeated in title matches in the city.

But not for the first time in the French capital, Alcaraz won the title by saving match points en route – this time against Taylor Fritz in the quarterfinals in scenes reminiscent of his iconic Roland Garros final win against Italian Sinner last year.

For world number four Shelton, it was a first defeat in a Masters final after winning his two previous appearances in showpiece matches at that level – both coming in the last two editions of the Canadian Open.
news.content: آلکاراز 7-6 (7/5)، 7-5 ست های متوالی را برای یک تاج دست نیافتنی پاریس قبل از فینال ATP پایان سال به دست آورد. کارلوس آلکاراز تا حدی از بن شلتون انتقام گرفت زیرا قهرمان هفت دوره گرند اسلم آمریکایی را با نتیجه 7-6 (7/5) شکست داد و 7-5 را شکست داد و اولین مردی را که در پایان فصل مسترز پاریس را برای اولین بار در مسابقات مسترز پاریس شکست داد. این بازیکن 23 ساله روز یکشنبه نهمین عنوان 1000 سطح حرفه ای خود را به دست آورد. برخلاف حماسه پنج ست یک چهارم نهایی آنها در نیویورک دو ماه پیش، درگیری در پاریس کمتر از دو ساعت به طول انجامید. آلکاراز پس از اینکه برای اولین بار جام توسط بوریس بکر، برنده سابق مسابقات مسترز پاریس تحویل شد، گفت: «هر سال به اینجا آمدم، بهترین تنیس خود را پیدا نکردیم اما هرگز تسلیم نشدیم. قبل از فینال ATP که از 15 تا 22 نوامبر در تورین برگزار می شود، الکاراز شماره سه جهان اکنون دارای پنج عنوان در سطح تور امسال است – تنها جانیک سینر مجروح با 6 عنوان قهرمانی بیشتر دارد. آلکاراز با ورود به پاریس پس از کسب عنوان 500 سطح در وین، 9 مسابقه آخر خود را برده است. در اولین دوره مسابقات قهرمانی ایتالیا خواهد بود. آلکاراز پس از دو قهرمانی اوپن فرانسه و اکنون مسترز پاریس، در مسابقات قهرمانی در شهر شکست نخورده است. اما نه برای اولین بار در پایتخت فرانسه، آلکاراز با حفظ امتیاز مسابقه در مسیر قهرمانی را به دست آورد - این بار مقابل تیلور فریتز در مرحله یک چهارم نهایی در صحنه هایی که یادآور خاطرات است.

news.originalContent:
Israel’s president officially tasks the opposition leader with forming a new government.

Israel’s opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, the man officially tasked by President Isaac Herzog with trying to form the country’s next government, has said that he was open to including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in his coalition lineup.

In a speech at Sunday’s ceremony in Herzog’s office in Jerusalem, Eisenkot suggested Netanyahu’s far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich was also welcome to join.

“If members of Likud and the Religious Zionist Party truly believe this is a time for unity, as they told the president, I cannot conceive of any reason why they would not support a government under my leadership and the principles I have presented,” Eisenkot said.

Eisenkot, who ran as Netanyahu’s main rival, has six weeks to form a new government. At the ceremony, Eisenkot said he will act in the interests of the public and represent all parts of Israeli society.

Herzog, meanwhile, warned that the country faced uncertainties after the November 3 midterm elections in the United States, which brought victories for several political figures critical of Israel and the US’s military support.

“The State of Israel needs a stable government,” Herzog said, pointing to the “new political reality” in the US.

Eisenkot led Israel’s military from 2015 to 2019 and sat as an observer in Netanyahu’s war cabinet for the first eight months of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, which began in October 2023.

Despite this, Arab-led parties endorsed Eisenkot for the mandate to replace Netanyahu.

In Israel’s October 27 elections, Eisenkot’s four-party alliance won 48 seats, while Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc secured 53, leaving both short of the 61 needed for a parliamentary majority. Arab-led parties, representing Palestinian citizens of Israel, won a record 19 seats.

Eisenkot has ruled out forming a government with the Arab-led parties, which would give him a 67-seat bloc. Winning over the two ultra-Orthodox parties, United Torah Judaism and Shas, would give him exactly 61 seats.

He could also form a government with fewer than 61 seats if he wins a parliamentary confidence vote.

“Netanyahu still has time to derail Gadi Eisenkot’s efforts to form a government and sabotage attempts to gain a vote of confidence,” said Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh, reporting from Ramallah, in the occupied West Bank.

“In the meantime, he remains caretaker prime minister. If Eisenkot fails, Netanyahu would be the natural second in line to be tasked with forming a government. And if he fails, elections would then be called, and that would still allow Netanyahu to remain as caretaker.

“Many of Netanyahu’s critics say that is his aim. The big question in Israeli politics now is: does the opposition really want to get rid of Netanyahu? Or is the opposition to Palestinian Israelis in mainstream politics so strong that they’re willing to risk keeping Netanyahu in power by going back to the ballot box?”
news.content: رئیس‌جمهور اسرائیل رسما رهبر اپوزیسیون را برای تشکیل دولت جدید موظف می‌کند. گادی آیزنکوت، رهبر اپوزیسیون اسرائیل، مردی که رسماً از سوی رئیس‌جمهور آیزاک هرتزوگ مأمور تشکیل دولت بعدی این کشور شده است، گفته است که آماده است تا بنیامین نتانیاهو، نخست‌وزیر اسرائیل را در صف ائتلاف خود قرار دهد. در یک سخنرانی در مراسم روز یکشنبه در دفتر هرتزوگ در اورشلیم، آیزنکوت پیشنهاد کرد که من بزالل اسموتریچ، وزیر دارایی راست افراطی نتانیاهو نیز از پیوستن به آن استقبال می‌کنم. «اگر اعضای لیکود و حزب مذهبی صهیونیستی واقعاً معتقدند که اکنون زمان اتحاد است، همانطور که به رئیس‌جمهور گفته‌اند، من نمی‌توانم هیچ دلیلی را تحت رهبری من ارائه دهند.» آیزنکوت گفت. آیزنکوت که به عنوان رقیب اصلی نتانیاهو نامزد شد، شش هفته فرصت دارد تا دولت جدید تشکیل دهد. در این مراسم، آیزنکوت گفت که در راستای منافع عمومی و نماینده همه بخش‌های جامعه اسرائیل عمل خواهد کرد. در عین حال، هرتزوگ هشدار داد که این کشور پس از انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای در 3 نوامبر در ایالات متحده با بلاتکلیفی مواجه شد که پیروزی‌هایی را برای چندین شخصیت سیاسی منتقد اسرائیل و حمایت نظامی ایالات متحده به ارمغان آورد. هرتزوگ با اشاره به «واقعیت سیاسی جدید» در ایالات متحده گفت: «دولت اسرائیل به یک دولت باثبات نیاز دارد.» آیزنکوت ارتش اسرائیل را از سال 2015 تا 2019 رهبری کرد و به عنوان ناظر در کابینه جنگ نتانیاهو در هشت ماه اول جنگ نسل‌کشی اسرائیل علیه غزه که در اکتبر آغاز شد، حضور داشت.

news.originalContent:
Kozo Tashima believes he has a ’20 to 30 percent’ chance of winning the FIFA presidency election against Infantino.

The latest challenger to FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s re-election bid, Kozo Tashima, believes he has a 20 to 30 percent chance of winning the coveted seat in global football.

Tashima, the honorary president of the Japan Football Association (JFA), said governance is FIFA’s biggest problem as he outlined his platform for next year’s presidential election on Sunday.

“I’ve received many messages saying, ‘Thank you for speaking out’…,” Tashima told Japanese daily Sports Nippon.

Tashima announced on Thursday that he intended to run in the March election, becoming the first Japanese candidate to seek world football’s top job.

The 68-year-old former Japan international has served on the FIFA Council since 2015 and became JFA president the following year before being succeeded by Tsuneyasu Miyamoto in 2024.

“I’ve been contacted by presidents and international department officials from eight countries, including some outside Asia,” he said.

“While I haven’t received any formal endorsements yet, I’m getting a positive response. Since time is short and I don’t want to be held up by incomplete paperwork, I want to secure support from at least six associations.”

Tashima requires nominations from five national associations, a prerequisite for standing in the election.

Candidates have until November 18 to submit nominations for the election, in which Infantino is seeking a fourth term as head of world football’s governing body.

Infantino came under scrutiny in July after an unsuccessful attempt to bring private investors into a new FIFA commercial entity holding rights linked to competitions including the World Cup.

Despite the criticism, Infantino’s candidacy received a significant boost in October when the head of Asian football publicly endorsed him, while support from several FIFA confederations has left him well placed among the organisation’s 211 member associations.

“I’ll keep what’s good and change what’s bad…,” Tashima added. “The biggest problem, however, remains governance…

“Selflessness is my motto… At this stage, I think my chances of winning are about 20 to 30 percent, but as the campaign progresses, I want to raise my confidence to 40 or 50 percent. I truly want to change FIFA.”

Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega was the first candidate to publicly declare his intention to challenge fellow Swiss citizen Infantino last month.
news.content:
کوزو تاشیما بر این باور است که او 20 تا 30 درصد شانس پیروزی در انتخابات ریاست فیفا در برابر اینفانتینو دارد. کوزو تاشیما، آخرین رقیب نامزد مجدد جیانی اینفانتینو، رئیس فیفا، معتقد است که او 20 تا 30 درصد شانس برنده شدن کرسی مورد علاقه در فوتبال جهانی را دارد. تاشیما، رئیس افتخاری اتحادیه فوتبال ژاپن (JFA)، در حالی که او روز یکشنبه برنامه خود را برای انتخابات ریاست جمهوری سال آینده اعلام کرد، گفت که مدیریت بزرگترین مشکل فیفا است. تاشیما در گفت‌وگو با روزنامه ژاپنی اسپورت نیپون گفت: «پیام‌های زیادی دریافت کرده‌ام که می‌گفتند: «از شما متشکرم... این ملی پوش 68 ساله سابق ژاپنی از سال 2015 در شورای فیفا خدمت کرده است و سال بعد رئیس JFA شد تا اینکه در سال 2024 سونیاسو میاموتو جانشین او شد. از آنجایی که زمان کوتاه است و نمی‌خواهم با مدارک ناقص درگیر شوم، می‌خواهم از حداقل شش انجمن حمایت کنم.»
تاشیما نیاز به نامزدی از پنج انجمن ملی دارد که شرط لازم برای حضور در انتخابات است. نامزدها تا 18 نوامبر فرصت دارند نامزدهای خود را برای انتخابات ارسال کنند، که در آن اینفانتینو حضور دارد.

news.originalContent:
Protesters seek tighter trade restrictions on Israel and a halt to all arms sales.

More than 200,000 people have taken to the streets of Amsterdam in the Netherlands, demanding government action against Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, according to the Dutch branch of Amnesty International, one of the organisers.

Sunday’s ‘Red Line’ protesters, many wearing red items of clothing, called for tighter trade restrictions on Israel and a halt to all arms sales.

“What is happening there is inhumane,” Mike van Dongen said as he walked in the huge throng of people.

“As far as I’m concerned, [the Dutch authorities] are doing nothing,” he said. “They don’t dare take any serious steps.”

As the protesters marched along a normally busy Amsterdam street that was closed to traffic on Sunday, a man stood at a bus stop with a loudspeaker shouting, “Free, free Palestine!” Many of the marchers echoed his cry as they passed.

Israel’s genocidal war has killed at least 74,000 Palestinians, including 21,000 children, since October 2023.

Sunday’s protest was similar to one in early October last year. That followed ‘Red Line’ demonstrations last June when protesters marched through the streets of The Hague.

A “ceasefire” took effect in Gaza on October 10 last year, but Israeli attacks and killings have continued on an almost-daily basis since.

The war in Gaza has strained relations between the Netherlands and Israel. The Dutch foreign minister resigned last year after failing to secure new sanctions against Israel.

Since then, a new minority coalition government took power in February and introduced an import ban on products from Israeli settlements, which the Dutch government and most of the international community consider illegal – the ban provoked a diplomatic spat with Israel.

Prime Minister Rob Jetten, who took part in a march last year but was not present on Sunday, defended his government’s actions at his weekly news conference on Friday.

“Every single day and every single week, we do what we can to alleviate the terrible situation there,” he said.

He added that his administration is “exerting greater political and diplomatic pressure” on Israel to abide by its agreements on Gaza.
news.content: معترضان به دنبال اعمال محدودیت های شدیدتر تجاری بر اسرائیل و توقف فروش سلاح هستند. به گفته شعبه هلند عفو بین الملل، یکی از سازمان دهندگان، بیش از 200000 نفر به خیابان های آمستردام در هلند آمدند و خواستار اقدام دولت علیه جنگ نسل کشی اسرائیل در غزه شدند. معترضان روز یکشنبه «خط قرمز» که بسیاری لباس‌های قرمز پوشیده بودند، خواستار محدودیت‌های تجاری شدیدتر بر اسرائیل و توقف فروش سلاح شدند. مایک ون دونگن در حالی که در میان جمعیت عظیم مردم قدم می‌زد گفت: «آنچه در آنجا اتفاق می‌افتد غیرانسانی است. آنها جرات هیچ قدم جدی را ندارند.» هنگامی که معترضان در امتداد یک خیابان معمولی شلوغ آمستردام که روز یکشنبه به روی ترافیک بسته بود راهپیمایی کردند، مردی با بلندگو در ایستگاه اتوبوس ایستاد و فریاد زد: «فلسطین آزاد، آزاد!» بسیاری از راهپیمایان فریاد او را هنگام عبور تکرار کردند.جنگ نسل کشی اسرائیل از اکتبر 2023 تاکنون دست کم 74000 فلسطینی از جمله 21000 کودک را کشته است. تظاهرات یکشنبه مشابه تظاهرات اوایل اکتبر سال گذشته بود. این به دنبال تظاهرات «خط قرمز» در ژوئن گذشته بود که معترضان در خیابان‌های لاهه راهپیمایی کردند. «آتش‌بس» در 10 اکتبر سال گذشته در غزه اجرایی شد، اما حملات و کشتار اسرائیل از آن زمان تقریباً به صورت روزانه ادامه یافت. جنگ در غزه روابط بین هلند و اسرائیل را تیره کرده است. وزیر خارجه هلند سال گذشته پس از ناکامی در تامین امنیت جدید استعفا داد

news.originalContent:
Celebrations feature fireworks, prayers, reunions, rangoli designs, feasting, and the sharing of sweets and gifts.

Diwali, the festival of lights, is being celebrated across India and among its vast diaspora, marking one of the most important days of the year for Hindus.

More than one billion people of different faiths take part in the celebrations in the world’s most populous nation, gathering for prayers, family reunions and the lighting of fireworks.

The name Diwali comes from “Deepavali”, meaning “a row of lights”, and many families place clay oil lamps outside their homes to symbolise the triumph of light over darkness and knowledge over ignorance.

The festival follows the Hindu lunar calendar and usually falls in late October or early November. This year, Diwali is marked on November 8.

While Diwali is rooted in Hindu tradition, it is also observed by Sikhs, Jains and Buddhists, with regional origin stories that share a common theme – the victory of good over evil.

Celebrations often include feasting, new clothes, rangoli floor designs, and the exchange of sweets and gifts with friends and neighbours.
news.content: جشن‌ها شامل آتش‌بازی، نیایش، گردهمایی مجدد، طرح‌های رنگولی، ضیافت، و اشتراک شیرینی و هدایا می‌شود. دیوالی، جشنواره چراغ‌ها، در سرتاسر هند و در میان مهاجران وسیع آن جشن گرفته می‌شود و یکی از مهم‌ترین روزهای سال را برای هندوها رقم می‌زند. بیش از یک میلیارد نفر از ادیان مختلف در جشن‌های پرجمعیت‌ترین کشور جهان شرکت می‌کنند و برای دعا، گردهمایی خانوادگی و روشن کردن آتش‌بازی گرد هم می‌آیند. نام دیوالی از «دیپاوالی» به معنای «ردیف چراغ‌ها» گرفته شده است و بسیاری از خانواده‌ها چراغ‌های نفتی سفالی را بیرون از خانه‌های خود قرار می‌دهند تا نمادی از پیروزی نور بر تاریکی و دانش باشد. این جشنواره از تقویم قمری هندو پیروی می کند و معمولاً در اواخر اکتبر یا اوایل نوامبر برگزار می شود. امسال، دیوالی در 8 نوامبر برگزار می‌شود. در حالی که دیوالی ریشه در سنت هندو دارد، سیک‌ها، جین‌ها و بودایی‌ها نیز آن را با داستان‌های منشأ منطقه‌ای مشاهده می‌کنند که موضوع مشترکی دارد - پیروزی خیر بر شر. جشن ها اغلب شامل ضیافت، لباس های جدید، طرح های کف رنگولی و تبادل شیرینی و هدایا با دوستان و همسایگان است.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

A former MAHA adviser is asking Susie Wiles and two Trump-linked lobbying firms to preserve records tied to the allegations he aired on Joe Rogan’s podcast.

Calley Means named Wiles, Ballard Partners and Continental Strategy in a post on X. He asked for records of meetings, policy calls and the access lobbyists were given, according to the post.

Means sought records involving Bayer, Monsanto and the glyphosate executive order, sugar-industry fundraising tied to federal nutrition policy, and lobbying invoices, meeting calendars and visitor logs. The request covers encrypted and disappearing messages, he wrote. (RELATED: White House Staffers Undermined Pesticide Reform Over ‘National Security,’ Former MAHA Adviser Alleges)

Means tied the move to reports that Wiles and former White House Deputy Chief of Staff James Blair were weighing a lawsuit over the interview, according to his post. Blair disputed that account on X, saying he warned Means he would consider suing if defamed. “Calley, your poor me act is tiring and embarrassing for a grown man,” Blair wrote.

In light of suggestions that Susie Wiles and James Blair may pursue legal action over my Joe Rogan interview, I am publicly requesting that she, Ballard Partners, Continental Straregy, and other relevant parties immediately preserve all potentially relevant records and communications, including: ✅All communications between Susie Wiles, Ballard Partners, and their representatives concerning lobbying access, meetings, policy decisions, and corporate clients. ✅All communications involving Bayer, Monsanto, Ballard Partners, and White House officials concerning glyphosate, the national security executive order, and the administration’s position in Supreme Court litigation involving Bayer. ✅All communications concerning sugar-industry political contributions, fundraising commitments, and discussions about how those interests related to federal nutrition policy. ✅All communications involving Tony Fabrizio, food-industry representatives, and White House officials concerning MAHA initiatives, school nutrition standards, and the proposed federal definition of ultra-processed foods. ✅All drafts, internal correspondence, meeting notes, and communications involving Walker Barrett, Heidi Overton, and other relevant officials concerning the glyphosate executive order and Bayer litigation, including discussions about Secretary Kennedy’s involvement. ✅All relevant lobbying agreements, invoices, payment records, meeting calendars, visitor logs, and communications concerning corporate efforts to influence the policy decisions discussed in my interview - including from Continental Strategy. ✅All nonprivileged communications concerning my allegations, their factual accuracy, and any contemplated legal action arising from my interview. This preservation request includes emails, text messages, Signal, WhatsApp, encrypted or disappearing messages, attachments, drafts, and relevant electronically stored records. I welcome a full and transparent examination of the facts.

The fight grew out of Means’ appearance on the “Joe Rogan Experience” released Friday. He resigned Oct. 22. Means said he quit over what he called corruption inside the administration.

Wiles told him she needed sugar-industry money to win the midterms, Means said in the interview, The Hill reported. He also described being handed the glyphosate order for review. Walker Barrett, the assistant to the president for policy, called it final and told him to tell Health and Human Services Secretary (HHS) Robert F. Kennedy Jr. that “this is not up for discussion,” Means said.

President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14387 on Feb. 18, invoking the Defense Production Act to secure domestic supply of glyphosate-based herbicides and elemental phosphorus, according to the Federal Register. The Supreme Court ruled 7-2 on June 25 that federal pesticide law bars state failure-to-warn claims against Monsanto, a Bayer subsidiary.

Means alleged Heidi Overton, now Trump’s FDA pick, worked with the Justice Department on why the court should take Bayer’s case, The Hill reported.

Spokeswoman Allison Schuster previously told the Daily Caller News Foundation (DCNF) the administration already secured extensive victories for the MAHA agenda. A White House official called Wiles essential to that work. She hands the job to Stephen Miller on Friday.

“I welcome a full and transparent examination of the facts,” Means wrote.
news.content:
(عکس از آنا مانی میکر/گتی ایماژ)
یکی از مشاوران سابق MAHA از سوزی وایلز و دو شرکت لابی مرتبط با ترامپ می‌خواهد که سوابق مرتبط با اتهاماتی را که او در پادکست جو روگان پخش کرده است، حفظ کنند. Calley Means با نام‌های Wiles، Ballard Partners و Continental Strategy در پستی در X. او درخواست کرد سوابق جلسات، تماس‌های سیاست‌گذاری و پست دسترسی به لابی داده شود. به دنبال سوابق مربوط به بایر، مونسانتو و فرمان اجرایی گلایفوسیت، جمع آوری کمک های مالی صنعت شکر مرتبط با سیاست تغذیه فدرال، و لابی کردن فاکتورها، تقویم جلسات و گزارش بازدیدکنندگان بود. او نوشت که این درخواست پیام های رمزگذاری شده و ناپدید شده را پوشش می دهد. (مرتبط: مشاور سابق MAHA ادعا می کند که کارکنان کاخ سفید اصلاحات آفت کش ها را به دلیل "امنیت ملی" تضعیف کردند) براساس پست خود، مینز این حرکت را با گزارش‌هایی مرتبط دانست که وایلز و جیمز بلر، معاون سابق رئیس کارکنان کاخ سفید، در حال بررسی شکایت بر سر این مصاحبه بودند. بلر با این حساب در X مخالفت کرد و گفت که به Means هشدار داده است که اگر بدنام شود، شکایت خواهد کرد. بلر نوشت: «کالی، رفتار بد تو برای یک مرد بالغ خسته کننده و شرم آور است. با توجه به پیشنهادهایی مبنی بر اینکه سوزی وایلز و جیمز بلر ممکن است در مورد مصاحبه جو روگان من پیگیر اقدامات قانونی شوند، من علناً از او، Ballard Partners، Continental Straregy و سایر طرف های مربوطه درخواست می کنم که فوراً تمام سوابق و ارتباطات بالقوه مرتبط را حفظ کنند، از جمله: ✅تمام ارتباطات بین سوزی وایلز، بالارد شرکا و نمایندگان آنها

جیمز بتز، محقق دانشگاه باث، درباره نحوه پردازش غذا و انرژی در بدن می‌گوید، یکی از عوامل مهم این است که «هورمون گرسنگی» ما، یعنی گرلین، معمولا اواخر روز بالاتر است: «هرچند وعده‌های غذایی معمولا این هورمون را سرکوب می‌کنند، این اتفاق در واقع فقط بعد از اولین وعده روز می‌افتد، نه بعد از ناهار یا شام.»

اما اینکه چه می‌خورید هم مهم است. غذاهایی که پروتئین و فیبر و حجم زیادی دارند، معمولا مدت بیشتری ما را سیر نگه می‌دارند.

آقای بتز می‌گوید که اگر شامتان مغذی و پروپیمان نباشد، ممکن است انرژی‌تان یک‌باره افت کند و همین باعث می‌شود سراغ تنقلات بروید.

بعضی‌ها هم از ترس اینکه نیمه‌شب گرسنه بیدار شوند دیروقت چیزی می‌خورند؛ عادت هم نقش دارد.

سوزان هیگز، متخصص اشتها در دانشگاه بیرمنگام، می‌گوید: «اگر خوردن تنقلات اغلب در یک شرایط مشخص اتفاق بیفتد، محرک‌های محیط می‌توانند هوس خوردن را برانگیزند. مثلا اگر کسی معمولا موقع تماشای تلویزیون تنقلات بخورد، فقط روشن کردن تلویزیون ممکن است هوس خوردن را در او بیدار کند.»

فقط حس گرسنگی نیست که اواخر روز بیشتر می‌شود. پژوهش‌ها نشان می‌دهد که اشتهای ما برای غذاهای پرکالری هم قوی‌تر می‌شود؛ اشتهایی که سیستم پاداش مغز آن را پیش می‌برد، نه نیاز واقعی به انرژی.

دکتر بولیو که هم در دانشگاه لیدز و هم در دانشگاه مونکتون کانادا کار می‌کند، می‌گوید: «علاقه و میل ما به غذاهای پرچرب، در مقایسه با غذاهای کم‌چرب، اواخر روز بیشتر است. این میل لذت‌جویی می‌تواند بر نشانه‌های سیری غلبه کند و باعث شود با اینکه سیریم، دلمان تنقلات یا دسر بخواهد.»

حتی بعد از یک شام مفصل، غذاهای شیرین یا چرب یا شور همچنان می‌توانند مسیرهای پاداش مغز را فعال کنند و همین توضیح می‌دهد که چرا خیلی‌ها باز هم دستشان به سمت خوراکی دیگری می‌رود.

پس اگر ساعت ۹ شب خودتان را جلوی بیسکویت دیدید، شاید مشکل کمبود اراده نباشد، این قوانین زیست‌شناسی‌ است که مقابل‌تان ایستاده است.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

شواهد ضدونقیض است اما قطعا خوردن غذای سنگین در دیروقت بر گوارش و آمادگی بدن برای خواب اثر می‌گذارد.

تنقلات چطور؟ اینجا نتایج پژوهش‌ها چندان روشن نیست.

شواهدی وجود دارد که غذاهای سرشار از کربوهیدرات‌های تصفیه‌شده و قندهای افزودنی، از نان سفید و برنج سفید گرفته تا بیسکویت و کیک، ممکن است با خواب بد ارتباط داشته باشند.

به نظر پژوهشگران، دلیلش این است که چنین غذاهایی نوسان‌های بزرگ‌تری در قند خون ایجاد می‌کنند و ممکن است برخی از پیام‌های هورمونی را که در تنظیم خواب و اشتها نقش دارند، تغییر دهند.

ولی تشخیص علت و معلول دشوار است و ممکن است برعکس باشد، شاید کسانی که بدخوابی دارند بیشتر سراغ تنقلات شیرین بروند.

جاناتان جانستون، متخصص خواب و ساعت بدن در دانشگاه ساری، می‌گوید: «می‌دانیم کم‌خوابی نه فقط اشتها را زیاد می‌کند بلکه میل به غذاهای پرانرژی را هم افزایش می‌دهد.»

به اعتقاد جیمز بتز، به همین دلیل نمی‌شود با قطعیت گفت که خوردن تنقلات در دیروقت خواب را به هم می‌زند یا نه: «شواهد اصلا روشن نیست و شاید نشان دهد که واکنش آدم‌ها به غذاهای مختلف پیش از خواب با هم فرق دارد.»

اول، ببینید چه چیزی شما را به خوردن تنقلات وامی‌دارد:

سوزان هیگز می‌گوید: «خوردن درحالی‌که حواسمان پرت است، مثلا موقع تماشای تلویزیون، می‌تواند باعث بیشتر خوردن شود چون کمتر به مقدار توجه می‌کنند.»

اما به باور دکتر بولیو، لازم نیست تنقلات شبانه را کاملا ممنوع کرد:

«اشکالی ندارد گاهی خوراکی‌هایی را که هوسشان را کرده‌اید، به اندازه بخورید.»

به گفته او، ترفند مناسب این است که مبنا یک انتخاب سالم باشد: «اگر خوردنی‌های وسوسه‌انگیز همیشه در کابینت نباشند و  اگر هستند گزینه‌ای سالم باشند، احتمال اینکه گزینه سالم‌تر را انتخاب کنید، بیشتر می‌شود.»

(Photo by Sean Gallup/Getty Images)

American soldiers need generators to run their radios and sensors, but the noise and heat can help enemy drones find them.

As drones and electronic warfare gear move down to small field teams, the Army and the Pentagon’s Defense Innovation Unit are turning to companies that build hybrid battery systems so troops can shut generators off.

“There’s no way to turn that off, or you’re kind of faced with this really bad decision, which is, you know, turn off the generator, but then lose all of my communications, all of my sensors, right, or leave it on and be a target,” Chariot Defense CEO Adam Warmoth, whose company makes hybrid power systems, told the Daily Caller News Foundation.

Republican North Carolina Rep. Pat Harrigan, who served in Afghanistan as an Army officer and sits on the House Armed Services Committee, said a unit’s efforts to stay hidden are wasted once an enemy drone senses the warmth of its generator.

“You’ve just given away your position,” he said in a statement to the DCNF.

Harrigan added that he is “absolutely interested in funding hybrid generators and battery systems that can take some of that risk off our soldiers” in the next defense bill.

“I want to know how much quieter they are, how long they can operate without resupply, and whether they can handle the demands of a combat deployment,” he said.

Harrigan led Democratic nominee Ashley Bell by about 3,000 votes in the Nov. 3 race for the 10th Congressional District, according to unofficial returns from the North Carolina State Board of Elections. He is set to hang on to his seat despite the nationwide blue tsunami causing a cascade of Democratic flips in the state.

The military’s standard-issue power sources “generate noticeable acoustic and thermal signatures,” which can make it harder for units to operate quietly, the Defense Innovation Unit wrote in a request for portable battery systems that closed in March.

“Generators are loud. They create a lot of visual signature. They create a lot of thermal signature, and we have to get past that,” Army Chief Technology Officer Alex Miller said at a defense industry conference near Detroit in August, Breaking Defense reported. (RELATED: The War Against The Machines Has Arrived)

Cummins, which makes the service’s Advanced Medium Mobile Power Source generators, did not immediately respond to the DCNF’s request for comment.

Warmoth, whose company is based in San Bruno, California, said one big lesson from Ukraine “is just how much electronic capability is needed.”

Command posts, sensors and counter-drone systems used to run from relatively safe areas in the rear, according to Warmoth.

“That’s all now getting pushed down to these mobile distributed units,” he added.

Not long ago, a platoon or company had only a couple of radios to keep charged, Warmoth noted. Now units are leaving their trailer generators behind because towing slows them down.

“That heat and noise that’s making them a target” is the other reason, he said.

Air conditioners, lasers and radars create “really high demands that end up sizing your generator,” Warmoth said.

“You end up bringing, say, a 30 kilowatt generator, which is 2,300 pounds, even though your average demand for power is maybe only two kilowatts,” he said.

An Army paper published in August 2025 found the same thing. During a training exercise for a 101st Airborne Division brigade, its 15- and 30-kilowatt generators frequently ran at less than 10 percent of capacity, the paper said.

“The problem is they never do the maintenance in the field on the generators because they can’t turn them off,” Warmoth said. “Because if they turn them off, they lose all their systems.”

Dan Grazier, a senior fellow and director of the national security reform program at the Stimson Center, said he saw the challenge firsthand as a Marine Corps tank officer in Iraq in 2007. At least eight big diesel generators powered Camp Fallujah, and his platoon escorted fuel convoys that kept them running.

“They’re big, they’re loud, and they’re necessary because the U.S. military travels with a lot of things that require electricity,” Grazier told the DCNF.

Artificial intelligence systems need far more power than traditional ones, so “this problem is only going to get worse,” he said.

Defense Logistics Agency Energy, which supplies the military’s fuel, sold about 152.2 million gallons for the Army’s needs in the first nine months of 2026, the agency said in a statement to the DCNF. It referred questions about generator use to the service. (RELATED: Homegrown Power Could Keep The Army Running If War Cuts Off Foreign Fuel)

Chariot’s answer is a battery system that stores power from the vehicles and generators units already have, Warmoth said.

The smaller Amphora 24 hooks into the jump-start port on U.S. and NATO military vehicles and charges while they drive, he said. When a vehicle “gets where it’s going, it can turn its engine off and run all the system silently.”

“We can charge off a vehicle in say three hours,” he added.

For a command post running basic communications and sensing gear, “you’re looking at say six to eight hours” of silent operation, Warmoth said.

Chariot sees about 50 percent fuel savings, though it “depends a little bit on the load,” he said.

“You’re looking at double the runtime just based on that fuel savings,” Warmoth added.

Because the system handles power surges, units “can actually bring a smaller generator, or no generator at all, and just use the vehicle as the generator,” he noted, adding that this leaves room to carry more fuel.

“A unit operating with Chariot equipment could potentially operate for 300 hours,” Warmoth said, using the example of a unit that could run 100 hours on generators and batteries alone.

Separately, trucks rigged to send power from their engines have cut fuel use in Army testing. In an Army experiment called Project Convergence, the trucks used nearly 50 percent less fuel than the three to six “underused standalone generator sets” units had been running, according to an article the service published in fall 2024.

Chariot announced in August that the Defense Innovation Unit had awarded it a contract to supply Amphora systems to Army brigades over 12 months, with deployments planned to begin in fall 2026.

Most of the money goes to buying systems that active-duty units take into the field and on deployments, Warmoth said. The aim is to learn how much power units really use, since “that data realistically doesn’t exist.”

John Webber, New Use Energy’s vice president of sales, said in a statement to the DCNF that he visited two 101st Airborne Division teams using the company’s portable power units in the field at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, in October.

He said each SunCase charged from one of the Army’s new Infantry Squad Vehicles could save about 44 gallons of diesel a week by the company’s own estimate, compared with idling the truck around the clock. The figure comes from one team whose equipment drew about 220 watts, he said.

“In short we would only add 3 hours of vehicle idle time every 24 hours,” Webber added.

If delivered fuel runs $8 a gallon, a SunCase that costs about $5,000 would pay for itself in roughly 14 weeks of field use, by Webber’s math.

So far, Army units have bought portable power a few at a time, New Use Energy CEO Paul Shmotolokha said in a statement to the DCNF.

“There have not been heavy buys of our product category in any formal program to date,” he said.

Lasers and similar weapons “are extremely energy intensive, which presents a logistics problem in particular for forward-deployed Army units relying on generators for power,” Wilson Beaver, senior policy advisor for defense budgeting and NATO policy at the Heritage Foundation, and co-author Ka’Von Johnson wrote in a June 2025 issue brief.

“When you’re standing outside the eJLTV in silent drive mode, all you hear is gravel,” Oshkosh Defense said of its hybrid Joint Light Tactical Vehicle in an Oct. 16 statement to the DCNF.

The company has shown the eJLTV, which offers silent drive and silent watch, to customers at home and abroad since its 2022 launch, an Oshkosh Defense representative said in a later statement to the DCNF.

Oshkosh also offers an exportable power kit for its Medium Tactical Vehicle Replacement truck that draws more than 40 kilowatts from the vehicle’s built-in capacity, or upward of 80 with stacked inverters, according to the representative.

“The MTVR exportable power kit can replace a towed generator completely or pair with a towed generator to supplement additional power when needed,” the representative added.

Neither the eJLTV nor the truck kit has been fielded, the representative said when asked about the Army and the Marine Corps.

“However, both services have expressed interest in this type of capability,” the representative noted.

“Replacing legacy generators with battery-inverter systems reduces thermal and acoustic detection risks,” the August 2025 Army paper said.

In a 2024 training rotation in the Pacific, small teams from a 25th Infantry Division brigade “operated for 56 to 96 hours” on one battery module and one power distribution module “without relying on generators or vehicles,” according to the paper.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

The Democratic sweep of the 2026 midterms has a bipartisan energy permitting deal racing the clock — and it puts President Donald Trump’s nuclear agenda under new overseers.

A procedural vote on the deal is set for about 5:30 p.m. on Nov. 9, according to the Senate’s calendar, and come January, Democrats will run the committees that oversee the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC). In an NBC News exit poll, voters very worried about utility and fuel costs went for Democrats by roughly two to one, and Chinese solar and battery stocks surged after the results.

“This is the closest we have come to actually finding something that can get signed into law, and I’m not going to wait,” Democratic New Mexico Sen. Martin Heinrich, who helped write the deal, said in a Nov. 4 statement to Reuters.

Democratic Rhode Island Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse called the bill “a bird in the hand” in his own statement to the outlet.

“We’d be fools not to take it,” he noted.

Heinrich and Whitehouse hammered out the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act with Republican West Virginia Sen. Shelley Moore Capito and Republican Utah Sen. Mike Lee, Reuters reported. Its goal is faster federal sign-off on power lines and mines, along with fossil fuel and renewable energy projects.

Capito introduced the bill Sept. 30. It went to the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, according to Congress.gov.

Outgoing Senate Majority Leader South Dakota Sen. John Thune filed on the same day to cut off debate on taking up H.R. 2347, a House bill that the Senate press gallery describes as “the legislative vehicle for the permitting reform bill.” (RELATED: Senators Want To Make AI Data Centers Pay For The Grid Upgrades Driving Up Your Electric Bill)

Jordan Nader, a resident senior fellow for energy and environment at the R Street Institute, said in a statement to the Daily Caller News Foundation that “a bill negotiated between committee leadership and agreed to by the White House is more certain than a hypothetical one.”

Nader said that if the bill fails, the next Congress would have to renegotiate it under new leadership. The administration has signaled support for the current bill, he noted, but its backing for a future one “is not assured.”

Tom Pyle, president of the American Energy Alliance, told the DCNF that a long fight over rewriting the deal could cost it Republican votes.

“If they spend an exorbitant amount of time renegotiating the deal, they run the risk of peeling off Republicans who swallowed pretty hard for some of the provisions that were priorities for Senator Whitehouse and Senator Heinrich,” Pyle said.

Investment firm TD Cowen cut its odds that the bill succeeds from about 40 percent to about 25 percent after the election, Reuters reported. The firm said the Democratic win “likely emboldens voices arguing bill gives too many concessions” to the oil and gas industry.

Democratic California Rep. Jared Huffman, the ranking member on the House Natural Resources Committee, is among those, along with environmental groups, who say the party can pass a more ambitious bill once it controls Congress, Reuters reported. Huffman did not immediately respond to the outlet’s request for comment.

Democratic Sens. Tammy Duckworth of Illinois, Ed Markey of Massachusetts and Jeff Merkley and Ron Wyden of Oregon said in an Oct. 27 letter that they were weighing whether to back the Nov. 9 vote, Newsmax reported. They urged the administration to first restore energy grants the Energy Department canceled in October 2025.

“In seeking our support for BAAJA, you are asking every Senator to rely on informal assurances from a Trump administration that has proven to be an untrustworthy and erratic negotiating partner and demonstrated a willingness to ignore and violate the plain language of the law,” they wrote.

Heinrich is the ranking member on the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, and Whitehouse holds the same post on the Environment and Public Works Committee, Newsmax reported.

Democrats won both chambers Nov. 3 and will hold at least 54 Senate seats, CBS News projected, with races in Alaska and Mississippi still uncalled.

Any bill the new Democratic majorities write would still need Trump’s signature or a two-thirds vote of each chamber to override a veto.

Pyle said Democrats have traded their climate message for one about high prices without changing their agenda.

“Unfortunately, none of their policies have changed,” he said. Pyle added that the “Democratic Congress will go after oil and gas companies, accuse them of price gouging” and hold “investigations and hearings.”

The offices of Heinrich, Whitehouse, Lee and Democratic New Jersey Rep. Frank Pallone, along with the Energy Department, did not immediately respond to the DCNF’s requests for comment.

Industry and right-leaning groups want the deal done now. “Congress doesn’t have to wait until 2027 to deliver,” Jeremy Harrell, CEO of the right-leaning clean energy group ClearPath Action, said in a Nov. 4 statement.

“Pass it before the 119th Congress adjourns,” Harrell added.

American Petroleum Institute President and CEO Mike Sommers wrote in an X article Nov. 4 that lawmakers “should finish the job and send the package to the president’s desk before the end of the year.”

“Election Day changed the balance of power in Washington. It did not change the energy equation: More supply. More infrastructure. More resilience,” Sommers wrote.

Permitting reform would give nuclear power an “incremental boost,” the consulting firm Wood Mackenzie said in a Nov. 4 release.

Changes that make it easier to build nuclear reactors are among the bipartisan priorities with a strong chance of passing the new Congress, Heatmap reported.

Trump ordered the NRC on May 23, 2025, to finish a “wholesale revision” of its regulations, with final rules due within 18 months. That window closes in late November.

The NRC has completed 10 rules under the order, according to its online tracker. The tracker shows later dates for 13 more rules in its final stage, 12 of them in 2027. The one modernizing reactor licensing, safety oversight and siting is listed for Feb. 26, 2027.

One of the completed rules, published in the Federal Register Nov. 3, sets deadlines for contested licensing hearings. (RELATED: Trump’s Nuclear Watchdog Puts A Clock On Legal Fights That Can Stall New Reactors)

Pallone, the ranking member on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, warned in prepared remarks for an April 22 hearing with the NRC’s commissioners that “it will be impossible for us to move forward on nuclear legislation as long as the NRC’s independence is in question.” The longtime New Jersey congressman is likely to chair the committee again when the Democrats assume control of the House in January.

He said in the same remarks that Trump “illegally fired” former NRC Chairman Chris Hanson in 2025.

Pallone also told the commission’s chairman in the same remarks that the chairman’s office “has been a model for transparency.”

“There’s going to be a lot more demand that these independent agencies regain their independence,” Paul Dickman, a former senior official at the NRC and the Energy Department’s National Nuclear Security Administration, told Heatmap.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Oct. 29 he hoped Michigan’s Palisades plant would restart before the end of November, WWMT reported.

Google signed a 20-year deal with Constellation in October backing 890 megawatts of new capacity at 11 existing reactors, and Constellation plans to invest more than $4.3 billion in them, the American Nuclear Society reported.

The Energy Department closed on as much as $1.9 billion in loan financing in September to restart Iowa’s Duane Arnold plant, which still needs NRC licensing approvals, according to the department.

Fifty-three percent of voters said they were very concerned about what they pay for utilities, and those voters backed Democratic House candidates 66 percent to 32 percent, according to the NBC News exit poll.

Fifty-nine percent of voters said they were very concerned about what they pay for gasoline and diesel, and that group also backed Democratic House candidates 66 percent to 32 percent, the poll found.

Seventy-six percent of voters opposed a new data center being built where they live, the poll found. NBC News combined Election Day interviews in 45 states with mail, phone and online surveys of early voters. Its results page does not list a margin of error.

Travis Fisher, director of energy and environmental policy studies at the libertarian Cato Institute, said in a statement to the DCNF on data center moratoriums that the Nov. 3 results and exit polls “sent a clear message: Americans reject data centers in their communities, especially if they bring higher electricity bills.”

“However, data center bans are a blunt instrument that would reduce upward pressure on utility bills but crush economic growth. There is a better way to address voters’ concerns,” Fisher added.

“If policymakers create a new pathway for large industrial customers like data centers to build their own power, at their own risk, on their own dime, they can welcome a growing industrial base without sticking everyday consumers with the bill,” he said.

Chinese clean energy stocks jumped Nov. 5 on bets that a Democratic Congress would boost support for clean energy, Reuters reported. Renewable stocks in the U.S. climbed as well.

Morningstar analyst Cheng Wang said that the Chinese rally owed more to investor sentiment than to concrete proposals, according to Reuters.

In Shanghai, the STAR new energy index was up 6.46 percent before midday. Battery maker CATL gained 5.17 percent, the outlet reported.

انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای 2026 از سوی دموکرات‌ها دارای انرژی دوحزبی است که اجازه می‌دهد توافقی با سرعت تمام شود - و دستور کار هسته‌ای رئیس‌جمهور دونالد ترامپ را زیر نظر ناظران جدید قرار می‌دهد. رأی‌گیری رویه‌ای درباره توافق حدود ساعت 5:30 بعد از ظهر تعیین شده است. در 9 نوامبر، طبق تقویم سنا، و در ماه ژانویه، دموکرات ها کمیته هایی را که بر کمیسیون تنظیم مقررات هسته ای (NRC) نظارت می کنند، اداره خواهند کرد. در یک نظرسنجی خروجی NBC News، رای دهندگانی که بسیار نگران هزینه های آب و برق و سوخت بودند، تقریباً دو بر یک به نفع دموکرات ها بودند و ذخایر خورشیدی و باتری چین پس از نتایج افزایش یافت. سناتور دموکرات نیومکزیکو در نوشتن بیانیه ای به مارتین هاینریش گفت: "این نزدیک ترین چیزی است که ما به واقعاً یافتن چیزی که می تواند به قانون تبدیل شود، نزدیک شده است." رویترز. سناتور دموکرات رود آیلند. شلدون وایت هاوس در بیانیه خود این لایحه را «پرنده ای در دست» نامید. او خاطرنشان کرد: «احمق خواهیم بود اگر آن را نگیریم.» هاینریش و وایت هاوس قانون دو حزبی مقرون به صرفه بودن و مشاغل آمریکا را با شلی مور کاپیتو، سناتور جمهوری خواه ویرجینیای غربی و سناتور جمهوری خواه یوتا، مایک لی گزارش دادند. هدف آن امضای سریع‌تر فدرال در خطوط برق و معادن، همراه با پروژه‌های سوخت فسیلی و انرژی‌های تجدیدپذیر است. کاپیتو این لایحه را در 30 سپتامبر معرفی کرد. به گفته Congress.gov، این لایحه به کمیته انرژی و منابع طبیعی سنا رفت. سناتور جان، رهبر اکثریت سنای داکوتای جنوبی.

موج بارندگی‌های شدید که در روزهای اخیر بخش‌های مختلف ایران را فراگرفته است، همچنان ادامه دارد. این بارش‌ها در شماری از استان‌ها موجب جاری شدن سیلاب، بالا آمدن سطح رودخانه‌ها، و اختلال در شبکه حمل‌ونقل شده و خسارات مختلف و شماری کشته و مصدوم بر جای گذاشته است. در همین حال گزارش شده که این بارندگی‌ها باعث پر شدن برخی سدهای ایران شده است. این بارش‌ها در چند روز آینده نیز بنابر پیش‌بینی‌ها ادامه خواهد یافت.

سازمان هواشناسی از بارندگی در ۲۵ استان، کاهش دمای هوا تا ۱۰ درجه در ۳۰ استان، و وزش باد نسبتا شدید تا شدید در ۱۰ استان کشور خبر داده است.

در استان‌های خوزستان، لرستان، چهارمحال و بختیاری، کهگیلویه و بویراحمد و کردستان از دیروز هشدار قرمز صادر شده است و کماکان ادامه دارد. برای تهران، البرز، قزوین، کرمانشاه، ایلام، زنجان و آذربایجان غربی هم هشدار نارنجی اعلام شده است.

در تهران نیز همزمان با ادامه بارندگی‌ها، مدیریت بحران نسبت به احتمال وقوع سیلاب و آب‌گرفتگی در نقاط مختلف پایتخت هشدار داده است.

علی نصیری، رئیس سازمان پیشگیری و مدیریت بحران شهر تهران، با اشاره به وضعیت جوی پیش رو اعلام کرده است که بارش‌های شدید می‌تواند به افزایش ارتفاع آب رودخانه‌ها، شکل‌گیری روان‌آب‌های گسترده، و آب‌گرفتگی معابر شهری منجر شود.

به گفته او، احتمال طغیان و سرریز شدن برخی رودخانه‌ها و کانال‌های آب نیز وجود دارد.

از صبح شنبه در تهران آب‌گرفتگی معابر گزارش شده که باعث راه‌بندان‌های طولانی و قفل شدن ترافیک شده است و برخی سامانه‌های هشدار ونقشه شهرداری هم از کار افتاده‌اند.

سازمان مدیریت بحران تهران از ساکنان خواسته است تا از رفت‌وآمدهای غیرضروری، حضور در حاشیه رودخانه‌ها و مسیل‌ها، و فعالیت‌های کوهنوردی در روزهای آینده خودداری کنند.

امید محترمی، سخنگوی سازمان مدیریت بحران کشور، هم با اشاره به تداوم بارش‌ها از صدور هشدار قرمز برای سواحل شمالی کشور خبر داد.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

مجتبی لشگری، سخنگوی سازمان اورژانس کشور، نیز از جان باختن «چهار نفر و مصدومیت ۱۱ نفر» در پی حوادث ناشی از شرایط نامساعد جوی در فاصله روزهای جمعه تا یکشنبه، ۱۵ تا ۱۷ آبان، خبر داده است.

به گفته او، دو نفر از جان‌باختگان بر اثر برخورد صاعقه جان خود را از دست داده‌اند و مصدومان این حوادث در استان‌های کهگیلویه و بویراحمد، خوزستان و بوشهر گزارش شده‌اند.

او همچنین گفت که در این مدت حوادثی مانند سقوط درخت، گازگرفتگی، تصادف، انسداد راه، ریزش نمای ساختمان، سقوط تیربرق، آسیب به خودروها، و قطع موقت آب و برق و تلفن در برخی نقاط کشور رخ داد.

به گفته امید محترمی، سخنگوی سازمان مدیریت بحران، «از ۱۸۰ روستایی که دچار قطع برق شده بودند، برق ۱۴۰ روستا وصل شده است. همچنین آب‌گرفتگی ۱۳۰ واحد مسکونی با تلاش نیروهای هلال‌احمر و آتش‌نشانی تخلیه شد.»

در کنار خسارات و حوادث گزارش‌شده، بارندگی‌های شدید روزهای اخیر وضعیت تردد در جاده‌های کشور را نیز تحت تاثیر قرار داده و موجب انسداد برخی مسیرهای ارتباطی شده است. در حال حاضر بخش‌هایی از شبکه راه‌های کشور با مشکلاتی از جمله کاهش دید، لغزندگی سطح جاده‌ها، و اختلال در تردد ناشی از بارش‌های سنگین مواجه‌اند.

سخنگوی سازمان مدیریت بحران کشور در همین زمینه اعلام کرده است که راه‌های ارتباطی «۴۰ روستا» همچنان مسدود است.

از سوی دیگر، آمار ایستگاه‌های هواشناسی و باران‌سنجی کشور نشان می‌دهد که تا پیش از ظهر امروز، ۱۷ آبان، در حدود ۴۵۰ شهر و ایستگاه تحت پوشش شبکه پایش سازمان هواشناسی بارندگی ثبت شده است که در این میان ایستگاه هواشناسی کوهرنگ با ثبت ۱۶۴ میلی‌متر بارش، بیشترین میزان بارندگی را به خود اختصاص داده است.

موج بارندگی‌های شدید که در روزهای اخیر بخش‌های مختلف ایران را فراگرفته است، همچنان ادامه دارد. این بارش‌ها در شماری از استان‌ها موجب جاری شدن سیلاب، بالا آمدن سطح رودخانه‌ها، و اختلال در شبکه حمل‌ونقل شده و خسارات مختلف و شماری کشته و مصدوم بر جای گذاشته است. در همین حال گزارش شده که این بارندگی‌ها باعث پر شدن برخی سدهای ایران شده است. این بارش‌ها در چند روز آینده نیز بنابر پیش‌بینی‌ها ادامه خواهد یافت.

سازمان هواشناسی از بارندگی در ۲۵ استان، کاهش دمای هوا تا ۱۰ درجه در ۳۰ استان، و وزش باد نسبتا شدید تا شدید در ۱۰ استان کشور خبر داده است.

در استان‌های خوزستان، لرستان، چهارمحال و بختیاری، کهگیلویه و بویراحمد و کردستان از دیروز هشدار قرمز صادر شده است و کماکان ادامه دارد. برای تهران، البرز، قزوین، کرمانشاه، ایلام، زنجان و آذربایجان غربی هم هشدار نارنجی اعلام شده است.

در تهران نیز همزمان با ادامه بارندگی‌ها، مدیریت بحران نسبت به احتمال وقوع سیلاب و آب‌گرفتگی در نقاط مختلف پایتخت هشدار داده است.

علی نصیری، رئیس سازمان پیشگیری و مدیریت بحران شهر تهران، با اشاره به وضعیت جوی پیش رو اعلام کرده است که بارش‌های شدید می‌تواند به افزایش ارتفاع آب رودخانه‌ها، شکل‌گیری روان‌آب‌های گسترده، و آب‌گرفتگی معابر شهری منجر شود.

به گفته او، احتمال طغیان و سرریز شدن برخی رودخانه‌ها و کانال‌های آب نیز وجود دارد.

از صبح شنبه در تهران آب‌گرفتگی معابر گزارش شده که باعث راه‌بندان‌های طولانی و قفل شدن ترافیک شده است و برخی سامانه‌های هشدار ونقشه شهرداری هم از کار افتاده‌اند.

سازمان مدیریت بحران تهران از ساکنان خواسته است تا از رفت‌وآمدهای غیرضروری، حضور در حاشیه رودخانه‌ها و مسیل‌ها، و فعالیت‌های کوهنوردی در روزهای آینده خودداری کنند.

امید محترمی، سخنگوی سازمان مدیریت بحران کشور، هم با اشاره به تداوم بارش‌ها از صدور هشدار قرمز برای سواحل شمالی کشور خبر داد.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

مجتبی لشگری، سخنگوی سازمان اورژانس کشور، نیز از جان باختن «چهار نفر و مصدومیت ۱۱ نفر» در پی حوادث ناشی از شرایط نامساعد جوی در فاصله روزهای جمعه تا یکشنبه، ۱۵ تا ۱۷ آبان، خبر داده است.

به گفته او، دو نفر از جان‌باختگان بر اثر برخورد صاعقه جان خود را از دست داده‌اند و مصدومان این حوادث در استان‌های کهگیلویه و بویراحمد، خوزستان و بوشهر گزارش شده‌اند.

او همچنین گفت که در این مدت حوادثی مانند سقوط درخت، گازگرفتگی، تصادف، انسداد راه، ریزش نمای ساختمان، سقوط تیربرق، آسیب به خودروها، و قطع موقت آب و برق و تلفن در برخی نقاط کشور رخ داد.

به گفته امید محترمی، سخنگوی سازمان مدیریت بحران، «از ۱۸۰ روستایی که دچار قطع برق شده بودند، برق ۱۴۰ روستا وصل شده است. همچنین آب‌گرفتگی ۱۳۰ واحد مسکونی با تلاش نیروهای هلال‌احمر و آتش‌نشانی تخلیه شد.»

در کنار خسارات و حوادث گزارش‌شده، بارندگی‌های شدید روزهای اخیر وضعیت تردد در جاده‌های کشور را نیز تحت تاثیر قرار داده و موجب انسداد برخی مسیرهای ارتباطی شده است. در حال حاضر بخش‌هایی از شبکه راه‌های کشور با مشکلاتی از جمله کاهش دید، لغزندگی سطح جاده‌ها، و اختلال در تردد ناشی از بارش‌های سنگین مواجه‌اند.

سخنگوی سازمان مدیریت بحران کشور در همین زمینه اعلام کرده است که راه‌های ارتباطی «۴۰ روستا» همچنان مسدود است.

از سوی دیگر، آمار ایستگاه‌های هواشناسی و باران‌سنجی کشور نشان می‌دهد که تا پیش از ظهر امروز، ۱۷ آبان، در حدود ۴۵۰ شهر و ایستگاه تحت پوشش شبکه پایش سازمان هواشناسی بارندگی ثبت شده است که در این میان ایستگاه هواشناسی کوهرنگ با ثبت ۱۶۴ میلی‌متر بارش، بیشترین میزان بارندگی را به خود اختصاص داده است.

منبع تصویر، Agencja Wyborcza.pl/Reuters

تیراندازی مرد مسلحی که گمان می‌رود با گروه‌های راست افراطی ارتباط داشته است، در مرکز کراکوف موجب کشته شدن دست‌کم شش نفر و زخمی شدن بیش از ۱۰ نفر شد. او که هدف گلوله پلیس قرار گرفت در بیمارستان بستری است.

این تیراندازی وقتی پیچیده‌تر شد که پلیس هنگام بازرسی خانه مهاجم سه جسد پیدا کرد که بعد معلوم شد پدر و مادر و خواهر او هستند. نگاهی می‌کنیم به آنچه تاکنون از این واقعه می‌دانیم.

حمله کمی پیش از ساعت ۱۵:۰۰ به‌وقت محلی (۱۴:۰۰ به وقت گرینویچ) در میدان اصلی بازار کراکوف، دومین شهر بزرگ لهستان، آغاز شد؛ مرکز شهر که گردشگران زیادی به آن سر می‌زنند.

به گفته پلیس، مردی با خودرو وارد میدان شد و بعد از داخل آن بی‌هدف «به سمت مردم» تیراندازی کرد. تصاویر، صحنه‌های وحشت و فرار مردم را نشان می‌دهد و صدای شلیک به‌وضوح شنیده می‌شود.

در این حمله ظاهرا بی‌هدف، به سمت تراموای در حال عبور هم شلیک شد که شیشه‌هایش شکست اما به هیچ‌یک از مسافران آسیبی نرسید.

به گفته مقام‌ها، ماموران مسلح با شتاب خود را به محل رساندند، با مظنون درگیر شدند و ظرف سه دقیقه پس از آغاز حمله، او را با شلیک گلوله زخمی و متوقف کردند و جلوی کشتار بیشتر را گرفتند.

مرد ۲۵ ساله‌ مهاجم که بازداشت شد، به‌دلیل جراحت گلوله همچنان در بیمارستان است.

تصاویر تکان‌دهنده‌ای که بی‌بی‌سی وریفای (بخش راستی‌آزمایی بی‌بی‌سی) صحت آن را تایید کرد، لحظه‌ای را نشان می‌دهد که یک مامور پلیس با مظنون افتاده بر زمین روبه‌رو می‌شود و چند بار شلیک می‌کند. بعد خود مامور هم که ظاهرا زخمی شده است، به زمین می‌افتد.

شیشه مغازه‌های میدان آسیب دیده‌اند که به نظر می‌رسد ناشی از اصابت گلوله باشد و تکه‌های شیشه روی زمین پخش شده‌اند. مقام‌های شهر از ساکنان و گردشگران خواستند تا زمانی که تحقیقات ادامه دارد، از این منطقه دور بمانند.

پلیس اعلام کرد ماشین مظنون را که در تقاطع خیابان‌های دیتلا و استرادومسکا پیدا شد، برای یافتن مواد منفجره احتمالی بررسی کرد ولی چیزی نیافته است. ساکنان ساختمان‌های اطراف هم در جریان این عملیات از سکنه تخلیه شده بودند.

کشته شدن شش نفر، چهار زن و دو مرد، تایید شده است که یک تبعه بریتانیا هم میان‌شان است. سه نفر از قربانیان لهستانی‌اند و هویت دو نفر هنوز مشخص نشده است.

۱۶ نفر، از جمله پنج تبعه خارجی و دو مامور پلیس و خود مهاجم، به بیمارستان منتقل شدند. وزارت کشور بعدا گفت که این اتباع خارجی اهل اتریش، بریتانیا، آلمان، پرتغال و روسیه‌اند.

دونالد توسک، نخست‌وزیر لهستان، بعدا نام دو پلیس زخمی را یاکوب کولیک و آرتور مورانسکی اعلام کرد.

یکی از وزیران لهستان گفت، حال یکی از این ماموران که هنگام بازداشت مهاجم سه گلوله خورد، «بسیار وخیم» است. به گفته او، این مامور تحت عمل جراحی است. مقام‌های لهستان نام و سن دیگر قربانیان را اعلام نکرده‌اند.

آقای توسک گفت که پلیس هنگام بازرسی خانه مرد مسلح پس از حمله، سه جسد پیدا کرده است، دو زن و یک مرد. پلیس لهستان روز یکشنبه تایید کرد این سه نفر پدر و مادر و خواهر ۲۱ ساله مرد مسلح بوده‌اند.

تحقیقات درباره مرگ این سه نفر ادامه دارد اما بر اساس گزارش‌ها ظاهرا با گلوله به قتل رسیده‌اند.

پلیس مهاجم را مردی ۲۵ ساله و لهستانی معرفی کرده اما نامش را اعلام نکرده است.

به گفته سخنگوی پلیس، مظنون «لباسی شبیه لباس نظامی» پوشیده بود و سلاح رده نظامی در اختیار داشت. با این حال، مقام‌ها گفته‌اند که او نظامی نبوده است.

این سخنگو همچنین گفت: «تعداد زیادی سلاح و مهمات در خودرویش پیدا شد.»

رسانه‌های لهستان گزارش داده‌اند که مظنون مجوز حمل سلاح داشت و شاید سلاح‌ها را از خانه‌ای که خانواده‌اش در آن زندگی می‌کردند، برداشته باشد.

یکی از وزیران گفت که تحقیقات اولیه نشان می‌دهد او یک «ملی‌گرای افراطی» است که از «ایدئولوژی‌های راست افراطی» الهام گرفته است اما جزئیات بیشتری نداد.

ماموران با پشتیبانی پلیس ضدتروریسم، خانه او را در اوستروویتس شوینتوکشیسکی، شهری در حدود ۲۰۰ کیلومتری کراکوف، بازرسی کرده‌اند.

تیراندازی در یکی از بزرگ‌ترین میدان‌های اروپای قرون وسطی رخ داد که شلوغ و محبوب گردشگران است.

جاناتان بالشا، اهل ایپسویچ، با دوست‌دختر لهستانی‌اش دومینیکا آنجا بود. وقتی تیراندازی شروع شد، آن دو بیرون کلیسای جامع سنت مری در گوشه میدان بودند.

جاناتان گفت: «از کنار کلیسا دویدیم، از در جانبی وارد شدیم و همراه چند نفر دیگر پنهان شدیم تا صدای تیراندازی خوابید. گلوله‌های زیادی شلیک شد، بیش از ۲۰ گلوله، و صدایش طوری بود که انگار چند سلاح مختلف به کار رفته است؛ دو صدای کاملا متفاوت شنیده می‌شد.»

دونالد توسک، نخست‌وزیر لهستان، پس از سفر به کراکوف گفت: «تا امروز در لهستان چنین مورد شدیدی از تروریسم نداشته‌ایم... و باید با همین عنوان از این حمله بی‌رحمانه به جان مردم در کراکوف یاد کنیم.»

اووکاش گیباوا، شهردار کراکوف، فرمانی امضا کرد که بر اساس آن، تا چهارشنبه ۱۱ نوامبر در شهر عزای عمومی اعلام شده است.

اندی برنام، نخست‌وزیر بریتانیا، گفت: «از تیراندازی هولناک امروز در کراکوف شوکه و اندوهگینم. دلم همراه خانواده جان‌باختگان، همه زخمی‌ها و همه کسانی است که از این خشونت بی‌معنا آسیب دیده‌اند. بریتانیا در کنار مردم لهستان ایستاده است.»

کایا کالاس، مسئول سیاست خارجی اتحادیه اروپا، گفت که این تیراندازی «فاجعه‌ای است که تاثیرش بسیار فراتر از لهستان حس خواهد شد.»

ولودیمیر زلنسکی، رئیس‌جمهور اوکراین، همسایه لهستان، این تیراندازی را «تکان‌دهنده» خواند و در شبکه‌های اجتماعی نوشت: «از طرف مردم اوکراین و از طرف خودم، صمیمانه به خانواده‌ها و عزیزان قربانیان تسلیت می‌گویم.»
